210	/**
211	 * A component for fetching and rendering product recommendations from the Einstein API
212	 * by a zone or a recommender name.
213	 */
214	const RecommendedProducts = ({
215	  zone,
216	  recommender,
217	  products,
218	  title,
219	  shouldFetch,
220	  ...props
221	}: RecommendedProductsProps) => {
222	  const { isLoading, recommendations, getZoneRecommendations, getRecommendations, sendClickReco, sendViewReco } =
223	    useEinstein();
224	  const { data: customer } = useCurrentCustomer();
225	  const { customerId } = customer;
226	  const { data: wishlist } = useWishList();
227	  const dataCloud = useDataCloud();
228	
229	  const createCustomerProductListItem = useShopperCustomersMutation('createCustomerProductListItem');
230	  const deleteCustomerProductListItem = useShopperCustomersMutation('deleteCustomerProductListItem');
231	  const toast = useToast();
232	  const navigate = useNavigation();
233	  const intl = useIntl();
234	  // Same split product-list/productListCardMapper.ts's own consumer uses
235	  // (product-list/index.tsx): passed into the mapper rather than formatted there, keeping that
236	  // mapper free of any react-intl dependency of its own.
237	  const formatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => intl.formatNumber(amount, { style: 'currency', currency });
238	
239	  const ref = useRef();
240	  const isOnScreen = useIntersectionObserver(ref, { useOnce: true });
241	  const [_products, setProducts] = useState(products);
242	  // Cart-exclusion check (2026-09-10, Marcel: "no recently viewed on cart" — a standing product
243	  // decision, not an Einstein-not-deployed-yet placeholder). Cart has no Zimmermann override
244	  // (no overrides/app/pages/cart/ at all) — its base page imports this same overridden component
245	  // and passes `recommender={EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED}`, which resolves to the
246	  // exact same string as PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED (confirmed identical,
247	  // node_modules/.../constants.js:154-160), so the recommender check below cannot tell the two
248	  // apart by value alone. `.endsWith('/cart')`, not an exact match — AGENTS.md's Multi-site
249	  // section: a real storefront path is locale/site-prefixed (e.g. `/en-GB/cart`), so an exact
250	  // `=== '/cart'` would only ever match the default site.
251	  const location = useLocation();
252	  const isCartPage = location.pathname.endsWith('/cart');
253	  // The See-Full-History trigger threshold, resolved for whichever breakpoint is actually
254	  // current. Also unconditional per rules of hooks; only meaningful inside the Recently-Viewed
255	  // branch below, same as `useLocation()` immediately above (whose derived `isCartPage` is read in
256	  // the fetch effect below too, as of the 2026-09-15 Cart-skip fix, in addition to the
257	  // Recently-Viewed branch further down). Reads the current breakpoint only — no ResizeObserver, no
258	  // runtime DOM measurement, matching the AC's own viewport-relative "exceeds the visible rail
259	  // width" wording (Open Question 1). See the module docblock's own "See-Full-History link"
260	  // section for why this is no longer a plain `useBreakpointValue` call.
261	  const visibleCardCount = useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount();
262	  // `buildUrl` site/locale-prefixes an internal path (e.g. `/en-GB/recently-viewed` on a non-AU
263	  // storefront) — AGENTS.md's Multi-site section: never assume routing. The rail itself must not
264	  // build this prefix; this container does it once, here.
265	  const { buildUrl } = useMultiSite();
266	
267	  useEffect(() => {
268	    // Cart-exclusion, extended to the fetch itself (2026-09-15, CodeRabbit finding, personally
269	    // verified before treating as valid). The Recently-Viewed render branch below already returns
270	    // `null` unconditionally on Cart for this recommender (see `isCartPage`'s own comment above),
271	    // so this request's result is never rendered on that route -- this skips firing it in the
272	    // first place instead of fetching a result nothing will ever read. Named in the build plan as
273	    // an accepted, optional cleanup ("the implementer may keep a Cart-only skip in the effect if
274	    // trivial"); it is.
275	    if (isCartPage && recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED) {
276	      return;
277	    }
278	
279	    // Check if the component should fetch results or not. This is useful
280	    // when you are still waiting on additional data, like `products`.
281	    if (typeof shouldFetch === 'function' && !shouldFetch()) {
282	      return;
283	    }
284	
285	    // Fetch either zone or recommender, but not both. If a zone and recommender
286	    // name are both provided, `zone` takes precendence.
287	    if (zone) {
288	      getZoneRecommendations(zone, _products);
289	      return;
290	    }
291	    if (recommender) {
292	      getRecommendations(recommender, _products);
293	      return;
294	    }
295	  }, [zone, recommender, _products, isCartPage]);
296	
297	  useEffect(() => {
298	    // This is an optimization that eliminates superfluous rerenders/fetching by
299	    // keeping a copy of the `products` array prop in state for shallow comparison.
300	    if (!Array.isArray(products)) {
301	      return;
302	    }
303	    if (products.length !== _products?.length || !products.every((val, index) => val === _products?.[index])) {
304	      setProducts(products);
305	    }
306	  }, [products]);
307	
308	  useEffect(() => {
309	    if (isOnScreen && recommendations?.recs) {
310	      // PostBuild fix round, Fix 1 (2026-09-15): Recently-Viewed only, report just the recs that
311	      // actually survived `selectRecentlyViewedCard`'s own null-filtering below — the same set the
312	      // render branch further down turns into `cards` — not the full raw `recommendations.recs`.
313	      // Every other recommender has no filtering step at all between its raw recs and what
314	      // actually renders, so the `else` branch below is the exact original, unchanged expression —
315	      // this `ids` computation changes nothing for them.
316	      //
317	      // Without this, a Recently-Viewed rec that fails to map (e.g. no usable name/image — see
318	      // that mapper's own hard-gate contract) still got reported to Einstein/DataCloud as
319	      // "viewed" even though the rail never actually rendered it: if every one of a shopper's
320	      // recently-viewed products failed to map, the rail correctly rendered nothing, but this
321	      // effect still told Einstein/DataCloud the shopper viewed every one of them — false signal
322	      // into Einstein's own recommendation-quality feedback loop, and silent (nothing on screen
323	      // indicated it happened).
324	      //
325	      // Recomputing `selectRecentlyViewedCard` here rather than sharing the render branch's own
326	      // `cards` (declared later in this same function, out of this effect's reach) is an accepted,
327	      // cheap duplicate — this effect only ever fires once per mount, since `isOnScreen` is itself
328	      // `useOnce: true` (use-intersection-observer.js). `recommender`/`formatPrice`/`buildUrl` are
329	      // read here without being added to the dependency array below, matching this same effect's
330	      // pre-existing omission of `sendViewReco`/`dataCloud` — `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` is off
331	      // repo-wide (see recentlyViewed/index.tsx's own docblock for the exact config line), and
332	      // `formatPrice`/`buildUrl` are recreated every render, so adding them would make this effect
333	      // re-fire on every render instead of once per mount.
334	      const ids: { id?: string }[] =
335	        recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED
336	          ? recommendations.recs
337	              .map((product: RecentlyViewedProduct) => selectRecentlyViewedCard(product, formatPrice, buildUrl))
338	              .filter((card: RecentlyViewedCard | null): card is RecentlyViewedCard => card !== null)
339	              .map((card: RecentlyViewedCard) => ({ id: card.id }))
340	          : recommendations.recs.map((rec: { id?: string }) => ({ id: rec.id }));
341	
342	      // Recently-Viewed only: nothing survived the mapping above, so nothing actually rendered —
343	      // report no impression at all, rather than an empty-but-still-sent call. Gated on the
344	      // recommender check too, not just `ids.length`, so the other four recommenders keep firing
345	      // unconditionally exactly as before, even in the (untouched, pre-existing) case where their
346	      // own raw `recs` happens to be an empty array.
347	      if (recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED && ids.length === 0) {
348	        return;
349	      }
350	
351	      sendViewReco(
352	        {
353	          recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
354	          __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,
355	        },
356	        ids,
357	      );
358	      dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations(
359	        {
360	          recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
361	          __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,
362	        },
363	        ids,
364	      );
365	    }
366	  }, [isOnScreen, recommendations]);
367	
368	  // SFCC-83 — Recently Viewed only. Every other recommender falls through to the unchanged
369	  // ProductScroller branch below. This branch sits ahead of the base dead-check below (see this
370	  // file's own module docblock, point 3, for why that no longer strictly matters but is kept
371	  // anyway) — every path inside this `if` returns on its own, so it never falls through to that
372	  // dead-check or the ProductScroller return regardless. Every other recommender is unaffected:
373	  // they still hit the exact same dead-check + ProductScroller path below, unchanged, just after
374	  // this check now short-circuits past them when it applies.
375	  if (recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED) {
376	    // Cart exclusion (2026-09-10, Marcel) — see the isCartPage constant's own comment above for
377	    // why this can't be expressed as a distinct recommender value. No rail, no title, no
378	    // placeholder — same treatment as the empty-state gate below, just for a different reason.
379	    if (isCartPage) {
380	      return null;
381	    }
382	
383	    // AC 8's empty-state gate, now against Einstein's own recs directly (build plan step E1) —
384	    // see this file's own module docblock for why this one check covers both the loading case
385	    // (`recs` undefined until `getRecommendations` resolves) and the true zero-history case. No
386	    // rail, no title, no placeholder.
387	    if (!recommendations?.recs?.length) {
388	      return null;
389	    }
390	
391	    // `recommendations.recs` is `useEinstein()`'s own untyped (`any`) result — like the
392	    // `.find`/`.some`/`.map` callbacks elsewhere in this file that already read off it, the
393	    // mapping callback below needs an explicit parameter-type annotation to satisfy
394	    // `noImplicitAny`. `RecentlyViewedProduct` (recentlyViewedCard.ts's own alias for
395	    // `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`) is reused here rather than a hand-rolled inline shape, since
396	    // it already names every field `selectRecentlyViewedCard` reads, and this input is a strict
397	    // superset of it (see the module docblock above).
398	    //
399	    // `buildUrl` (already in scope above, for `seeAllHref`) is now also passed into the mapper
400	    // itself (2026-09-15, CodeRabbit finding, confirmed) — see selectRecentlyViewedCard's own
401	    // docblock: without it, every card's href was a bare, unprefixed `/product/:id` path, which
402	    // sent a non-default-site shopper to the default site/locale instead of the storefront they
403	    // were actually browsing.
404	    const cards: ZimmRecentlyViewedCardProps[] = recommendations.recs
405	      .map((product: RecentlyViewedProduct) => selectRecentlyViewedCard(product, formatPrice, buildUrl))
406	      .filter((card: RecentlyViewedCard | null): card is RecentlyViewedCard => card !== null)
407	      .map(
408	        (card: RecentlyViewedCard): ZimmRecentlyViewedCardProps => ({
409	          ...card,
410	          // Inert for this variation — ZimmProductCardContent never mounts when
411	          // variation: 'recentlyViewed' (zimmProductCard/index.tsx's
412	          // VARIATION_CONFIG.showContent). 'h3' matches the one other established value for
413	          // this same required field (product-list/productListCardMapper.ts).
414	          headingLevel: 'h3',
415	          variation: 'recentlyViewed',
416	        }),
417	      );
418	
419	    // The See-Full-History link, finally wired in (was a stated "not yet built" gap on every
420	    // caller until now). Triggers when the shopper has more recently-viewed products
421	    // than fit in view at the *current* breakpoint — matching the AC's own "exceeds the visible
422	    // rail width" wording, which is viewport-relative, not a flat count. Compared against
423	    // `cards.length` (the full, unsliced count this container just built from Einstein's own
424	    // `recommendations.recs` — no client-side cap, build plan step E4 Open Question 4), not the
425	    // rail's own internal 5-item render slice, since the question is "does more exist than is
426	    // visible", not "did we cap the render".
427	    const showSeeAllLink = cards.length > visibleCardCount;
428	
429	    return (
430	      // Ref-attachment point — see the module docblock's own isOnScreen/forwardRef note above for
431	      // why this wrapper exists at all. `{...props}` forwards the caller's own layout props (e.g.
432	      // PDP's `mx={{base: -4, md: -8, lg: 0}}`, Cart's `mx={{base: -4, sm: -6, lg: 0}}`) exactly
433	      // as the ProductScroller branch below already does — without it, this branch would render
434	      // inset inside the page's normal content padding while every sibling rail on the same page
435	      // bleeds edge-to-edge, and zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own card-width math (e.g.
436	      // 201x2=402) assumes the full viewport width is actually available. `title` is passed
437	      // straight through with no `recommendations?.displayMessage` fallback — this component owns
438	      // no copy of its own for this branch (build plan A5/A6): the real title always comes from
439	      // the caller, regardless of whether Einstein's own `displayMessage` is present.
440	      <Box ref={ref} {...(props as BoxProps)}>
441	        <ZimmRecentlyViewedRail
442	          title={title}
443	          cards={cards}
444	          seeAllHref={showSeeAllLink ? buildUrl(RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE) : undefined}
445	          seeAllLabel={showSeeAllLink ? intl.formatMessage(messages.seeFullHistory) : undefined}
446	        />
447	      </Box>
448	    );
449	  }
450	
451	  // The component should remove itself altogether if it has no recommendations
452	  // and we aren't loading any.
453	  if (!isLoading && (!recommendations || recommendations.length < 1)) {
454	    return null;
455	  }
456	
457	  // TODO: DRY this handler when intl provider is available globally
458	  const addItemToWishlist = async (product: RecommendedProduct) => {
459	    try {
460	      if (!wishlist || !customerId) {
461	        return;
462	      }
463	      await createCustomerProductListItem.mutateAsync({
464	        parameters: {
465	          listId: wishlist.id,
466	          customerId,
467	        },
468	        body: {
469	          quantity: 1,
470	          productId: product.productId,
471	          public: false,
472	          priority: 1,
473	          type: 'product',
474	        },
475	      });
476	
477	      toast({
478	        title: intl.formatMessage(TOAST_MESSAGE_ADDED_TO_WISHLIST, { quantity: 1 }),
479	        status: 'success',
480	        action: (
481	          // it would be better if we could use <Button as={Link}>
482	          // but unfortunately the Link component is not compatible
483	          // with Chakra Toast, since the ToastManager is rendered via portal
484	          // and the toast doesn't have access to intl provider, which is a
485	          // requirement of the Link component.
486	          <Button variant="link" onClick={() => navigate('/account/wishlist')}>
487	            {intl.formatMessage(TOAST_ACTION_VIEW_WISHLIST)}
488	          </Button>
489	        ),
490	      });
491	    } catch {
492	      toast({
493	        title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE),
494	        status: 'error',
495	      });
496	    }
497	  };
498	
499	  const removeItemFromWishlist = async (product: RecommendedProduct) => {
500	    try {
501	      const wishlistItem = wishlist?.customerProductListItems?.find(
502	        (item: { productId?: string }) => item.productId === product.productId,
503	      );
504	      if (!wishlistItem || !wishlist || !customerId) {
505	        return;
506	      }
507	      await deleteCustomerProductListItem.mutateAsync({
508	        parameters: {
509	          customerId,
510	          itemId: wishlistItem.id,
511	          listId: wishlist.id,
512	        },
513	      });
514	      toast({
515	        title: intl.formatMessage(TOAST_MESSAGE_REMOVED_FROM_WISHLIST),
516	        status: 'success',
517	        id: product.productId,
518	      });
519	    } catch {
520	      toast({
521	        title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE),
522	        status: 'error',
523	      });
524	    }
525	  };
526	
527	  return (
528	    <ProductScroller
529	      ref={ref}
530	      title={title || recommendations?.displayMessage}
531	      products={recommendations.recs}
532	      isLoading={isLoading}
533	      productTileProps={(product: RecommendedProduct) => ({
534	        onClick: () => {
535	          sendClickReco(
536	            {
537	              recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
538	              __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,
539	            },
540	            product,
541	          );
542	        },
543	        enableFavourite: true,
544	        isFavourite: wishlist?.customerProductListItems?.some(
545	          (item: { productId?: string }) => item.productId === product?.productId,
546	        ),
547	        onFavouriteToggle: (toBeFavourite: boolean) => {
548	          const action = toBeFavourite ? addItemToWishlist : removeItemFromWishlist;
549	          return action(product);
550	        },
551	      })}
552	      {...props}
553	    />
554	  );
555	};
556	
557	export default RecommendedProducts;

  * SFCC-83 — the Recently Viewed rail organism (build plan section A5). Purely presentational:
  * data arrives as props, no data-fetching, no `useEinstein`, no `useIntl` — see
  * .claude/rules/components.md's container/presentational split. The container (A6) is
- * responsible for building `cards` (via A3's Einstein-rec-to-card mapper), gating this
- * component's visibility (A4's `hasRecentlyViewed`), and supplying `title`/`seeAllLabel` copy.
+ * responsible for building `cards` (via A3's Einstein-rec-to-card mapper) and supplying
+ * `title`/`seeAllLabel` copy. **Corrected 2026-09-15 (PostBuild fix round, Fix 4):** this line
+ * previously credited "A4's `hasRecentlyViewed`" — the now-deleted `useRecentlyViewedHistory`
+ * hook — with gating this component's visibility, in the present tense, well after that hook was
+ * removed (build plan step E4). The real visibility gate has lived entirely in the container since
+ * build plan step E1 (`recommended-products/index.tsx`'s own `!recommendations?.recs?.length`
+ * check) — this component has never gated its own visibility beyond the `visibleCards.length === 0`
+ * guard below; it renders whatever `cards` it is given, or nothing.
  *
  * Structure mirrors Figma exactly: a `header` row (title left, the See-Full-History link right)
  * above a `group` of `ZimmProductCard`s. No rail-level arrow buttons — `ZimmProductCardMedia`
@@ -122,8 +128,13 @@ export const ZimmRecentlyViewedRail = ({ title, cards, seeAllHref, seeAllLabel }
   const maxVisibleCards = useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount();
   const visibleCards = cards.slice(0, maxVisibleCards);
 
-  // Second guard behind A4's own visibility gate, which lives in the container, not here — an
-  // empty rail renders nothing at all, not an empty shell.
+  // Guards against an empty/all-capped-out `cards` array — an empty rail renders nothing at all,
+  // not an empty shell. Corrected 2026-09-15 (PostBuild fix round, Fix 4): this used to describe
+  // itself as a "second guard behind A4's own visibility gate", A4 being the now-deleted
+  // `useRecentlyViewedHistory` hook's `hasRecentlyViewed` check (removed build plan step E4). The
+  // real visibility gate is the container's own `!recommendations?.recs?.length` check
+  // (`recommended-products/index.tsx`, build plan step E1) — this component has never gated its
+  // own visibility on anything besides this one check.
   if (visibleCards.length === 0) {
     return null;
   }

content.text:
## Score: `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed-einstein` — PostBuild fix round (Round 1 of the fix loop)

**Consequence if this round were wrong:** Einstein would keep getting told a shopper "saw" recommendations that were never actually on their screen — poisoning its own future recommendation quality, silently, with nothing in the UI to show it was happening. That's the bug this round exists to close.

**What I found:** it's closed, correctly, and I made myself prove it rather than take the round's own word for it.

### Per-axis table

| Axis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Pass criteria** | PASS | All 5 findings PostBuild sent back (🔴#1, 🟡#2/#3/#4, 🔵#5) are addressed in the diff; the one 🔵 named "out of scope" (#6, Full History page's tracking gap) is correctly untouched. |
| **Correctness** | PASS | `tsc --noEmit` clean (independently re-run), `npm run test -- --run` → 85/1310 green (independently re-run), `eslint` scoped to the 4 touched files → clean (I ran this myself; it wasn't in the original claim). No open 🔴. |
| **Design fidelity** | PASS (nothing to check) | Confirmed by reading the diff: zero JSX/props/style lines touched. The only code change is inside a `useEffect` that never renders anything; the other two files are comment-only. No rendered-output surface exists for this round to get wrong. |
| **Conformance** | PASS | TS-only, no new imports, no hardcoded design values, no bare token keys (none of this touches styling at all). The self-correcting docblock style used in Fix 2/Fix 4 ("earlier revision claimed X, that was wrong, here's why") matches this repo's own established convention (see `overrideStyling.md`'s and `testing.md`'s own "earlier revision... corrected" paragraphs) — not a violation of "don't remove comments," a sanctioned correction-in-place. |
| **Completeness** | PASS | Finding #3 explicitly asked for test coverage; it's there, and I mutation-tested it myself (below), not just read it. |
| **Restraint** | PASS | Exactly the 4 files the 5 findings implicate, nothing more. No re-running of already-settled E1–E4/CR-fix work, no drive-by refactor. |

**Overall: PASS**

### What I tried to falsify

1. **The "else branch is unchanged" claim** — I didn't accept it. I diffed the live file against `git show HEAD:overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx` myself. The non-RV branch's expression, `recommendations.recs.map((rec: { id?: string }) => ({ id: rec.id }))`, is textually identical to what was inlined twice before — it's now computed once into `ids` and reused for both `sendViewReco` and `dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations` calls. I went one step further than "identical text" and checked whether reusing one array *reference* for both calls (instead of two separately-computed arrays) could matter — i.e., does either callee mutate its `products` argument? I read both vendor implementations directly (`use-einstein.js:296-308`'s `sendViewReco` just spreads into a body object; `use-datacloud.js:351-370`'s `sendViewRecommendations` only `.map()`s, never mutates). Confirmed safe — no behavioural difference for the 4 unaffected recommenders.

2. **The mutation-test claim** — I re-ran it myself rather than trust the description. Saved this round's diff for `index.tsx` as a patch, `git apply -R`'d it to restore the file to byte-exact pre-fix state (verified against `HEAD` — empty diff), ran the new test file: the "every rec fails to map" test **failed**, and for the exact claimed reason — `sendViewReco` was called once with `rec-1`/`rec-2`, the two ids that never rendered. The sibling "any other recommender... unchanged" test still **passed** against the reverted code (correctly — it's testing behaviour the fix never touched). Reapplied the patch, confirmed the restore was byte-identical to the original, re-ran the full file (10/10), full suite (85/1310), and `tsc` — all clean.

3. **"No prior test touched this effect" claim** — checked the pre-round file (`git show HEAD:...`) directly: `use-intersection-observer` was mocked as `default: () => false` with zero overrides anywhere in the file, so `isOnScreen` was always false and `if (isOnScreen && recommendations?.recs)` never ran its body in any existing test. Confirmed true — nothing is now redundant or at risk of silent breakage.

4. **The `CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`/`PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` string-collision omission** — traced the actual mechanism rather than accepting the implementer's self-assessment. `ref` only attaches inside the RV render branch's `<Box ref={ref}>`, which sits *after* `if (isCartPage) return null`. On the Cart route, that `null` return fires first, `ref.current` never becomes a real node, `useIntersectionObserver`'s own `if (!ref?.current) return` guard means `isOnScreen` never flips true, so the new effect's `recommender === PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` branch can never execute there — regardless of the string collision. This is the same pattern the file already uses elsewhere (route-based, not recommender-value-based, disambiguation) for the fetch-effect Cart-skip and the render branch itself. **Verdict: correctly scoped, no fix needed this round.**

5. **Tier scope** — re-verified from scratch, not trusted from postbuild.md. This round's own 4 files: zero Tier 1, one Tier 2 surface (`recommended-products/`), matching what was pre-authorized. See below for a broader finding this turned up.

### What I could not verify

- Everything postbuild.md's own "Could not verify" section already names (Einstein undeployed everywhere, real BM recommender shape, real `IntersectionObserver` behaviour for a zero-area target) — unchanged by this round, not re-litigated.
- Whether the Tier 2 touches to `overrides/app/routes.tsx` and `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (found below, pre-dating this round) have been informally coordinated with their named owners already — that's a conversation, not something a diff can show me.
- CodeRabbit hasn't run against this round's code yet (no PR open) — expected at this stage, not a gap in what I certified.

### Defects

None found in this round that need rework.

### If PASS: biggest residual risk in shipping this step

The fix recomputes `selectRecentlyViewedCard` a second time inside the effect instead of sharing the render branch's own `cards` — an accepted duplicate, justified today because the effect only fires once per mount. If a future change ever adds a *further* filtering step to the render branch's `cards` (a dedupe, a cap, anything past the `selectRecentlyViewedCard` map/filter) without mirroring it into this effect's own copy, the two computations silently diverge again — the exact same class of bug this round just closed, from a different angle. Worth a one-line pointer in the render branch's own comment ("if you add a step here, mirror it at the effect above") so the next person doesn't have to rediscover this the hard way.
